commit.message:
Fix the gaps a second review found: masking, guard parsing, sandbox-check

A second cross-model review (Codex) of the previous commit confirmed its
fixes and proved nine more problems. This commit fixes eight of them.

- Shared masking (safe.py): masks quoted values with spaces, short
  values, values behind Unicode width forms or invisible characters, and
  keys next to non-ASCII letters. Every pattern now runs in linear time:
  a 20,000-character worst case takes about 20 ms, where before some
  shapes took over 30 seconds, and a 4,000-character tool name stalled
  the runaway-guard hook for 21 seconds.
- sandbox-check uses the shared masking and puts file names, targets,
  and system names in inline code; it had printed a settings file name
  as live HTML and masked nothing.
- rules-to-guards checks each relative path from the starting folder and
  from the folder after any cd, so a cd the hook gets wrong can only add
  a block. It checks heredocs fed to a shell, reads delimiters with
  punctuation, ends a heredoc only at an exact terminator, restores the
  old nesting depth, and shows full patterns in its preview.
- claim-check counts code and tests inside agent and editor folders,
  and data files under test folders, as edits.
- harness-test-drive takes harness labels and fix hints from its own
  table and puts task ids, unknown statuses, and fix sizes in inline code.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Keep untrusted text inert in every skill report; close guard bypasses

An audit of all ten skills found 22 places where text from a repository,
a settings file, an MCP server, or a session log reached a Markdown report
as live Markdown: links, HTML tags, and bare URLs rendered, and one
commit subject printed a password. The README promised this could not
happen.

- New shared skills/evals/shared/safe.py holds redact, safe_text, and a
  new code(), which masks secrets, keeps text on one line, and wraps it
  in inline code. sync_shared.py copies it into nine skills.
  harness-test-drive, tool-design-checker, and agents-md-checker drop
  their own weaker masking for it.
- Every skill except sandbox-check (already compliant) now passes
  untrusted values through code(). JSON data fields stay plain and
  masked. Each skill has the auditor's proof tests plus sweep tests.

A cross-model review (Codex) reproduced three more gaps:
- rules-to-guards checks commands inside unquoted heredocs, reads partly
  quoted delimiters, and follows cd and pushd across chained commands. A
  cd it cannot follow keeps the last known folder, so nothing it blocked
  before is now allowed.
- claim-check counts edits under hidden folders such as .github and
  .cargo after a passing run; it still skips version control, editor,
  and agent folders.

The eval README now says four automated checks run in CI, and the
behavior cases are for a fresh agent to run. The regression-finder
README names rollbacks as a limit.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Mark every MCP tool read-only; raise the SDK floor to 1.7 (0.7.1)

Every tool only reads, so each now declares readOnlyHint=True. Every
tool calls data(), which fetches harnesses.json from GitHub on a PyPI
install, so each also declares openWorldHint=True. A new test lists
every registered tool and checks both hints.

Tool annotations need MCP SDK 1.7 or later, so the floor rises from 1.2
to 1.7. The script header in server.py also gets the <2 upper bound that
pyproject already had: without it, `uv run <raw URL>` resolved mcp 2.3.0
and crashed on the fastmcp import.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Fix a test that passed only on paths with spaces; drop stale "past bugs" wording

The runaway-guard Codex install test expected a quoted guard.py path, but
shlex.quote adds quotes only when the path needs them, so the test failed
on the Linux CI runner. It now splits the command and checks the words.

The plugin description and a regression-finder link still said
harness-test-drive runs your "past bugs"; it runs tasks from your git
history, which include features and refactors.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Close the remaining gaps in the safe-settings guard hook

The reset, clean, checkout, restore, and branch -D rules now accept git
global options such as -C and -c, the same way the push rule does, and
checkout or restore of one ref over the whole tree is blocked. The
template also denies Edit on .claude/hooks so the agent cannot rewrite
its own guard. guardrail-tester now scores the template at 70 of 90.

The site copy buttons select the text when the browser blocks clipboard
access, and the plugin install commands use a plain code fence.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Regenerate README, harnesses.json, and llms.txt with the Skills section

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Safe-settings template: catch git -C and quoted force pushes; deny edits to hooks, settings, and startup files

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Add claim-check skill: did the tests really pass when your agent said so?

Finds every 'tests pass' or 'build passes' claim in Claude Code, Codex,
Gemini CLI, and OpenCode sessions and checks it against the transcript:
backed (a matching run passed and nothing changed after it), stale,
contradicted, unsupported, or unclear with the reason. Also flags
weakened tests in the current diff, and offers a Stop hook that sends
the agent back once per reply when its last run failed. Precision on
real sessions: 20 of 20 on an independent sample.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Add guardrail-tester skill: do your agent's guardrails hold?

Simulates the permission rules of Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode,
and Cursor against about 90 dangerous commands in the forms known to slip
past prefix rules, and with consent runs your own hooks on them one at a
time. Reports what is blocked, what only asks (and whether only the mode
asks), and what runs without asking, worst first, with grep patterns and
rules to close each gap. Replays recent real calls to measure friction.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Add agents-md-checker skill: what each coding agent really loads

Maps which instruction files Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode,
Cursor, GitHub Copilot, and Aider load from a folder, what each one cuts
or skips (such as Codex's 32 KiB budget, or Claude Code ignoring AGENTS.md
when a CLAUDE.md exists), and whether the documented commands still work.
With --run, only commands whose every resolved step is on a known-safe
list run, after the user sees the exact script and recipe lines.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Safe-settings template: block force-push refspecs, split rm flags, and writes to hook and startup files

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Wire skills into the README, site, llms.txt, harnesses.json, and MCP server (0.7.0)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Add regression-finder skill: find the update where your agent changed

Splits your Claude Code or Codex sessions by harness version, model, or
week, compares per-session behavior (reads before editing, reads per edit,
edits to unread files, tool errors, interrupts, corrections, output, cost)
with Mann-Whitney plus Fisher's exact test for sparse metrics and a
Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment, leaves out versions from a second install,
and names the confounders (model, project, session shape) at every flag.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Add harness-test-drive skill: test-drive coding agents on your own repo

Mines tasks from your git history (commits whose tests fail before the
change and pass after it, checked twice), runs Claude Code, Codex, and
Gemini CLI on each in a fresh copy that holds only the parent commit, and
scores the saved diff in a clean copy with the hidden tests restored.
Reports pass rate, minutes, and cost per pass, keeps a harness that could
not start out of the scores, and stops at a dollar cap you set.

Verified with a real capped run on this repo: Codex passed a 37-line
Pages build fix in 2.8 minutes at $1.04 (API list prices); a Claude Code
install with an expired login was reported as could not run, at $0.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Shared session parser: permission mode on tool calls, flag credentials masked

Claude Code tool events now carry the permission mode in effect (the latest
permissionMode on a user record), so a replay can use how each session
really ran. redact() also masks credentials passed as command flags:
sshpass -p, mysql -p<pw>, curl -u user:<pw>, and --password <pw>.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Add runaway-guard skill: stop loops and runaway spend mid-session

A hook for interactive Claude Code and Codex sessions, where
--max-budget-usd does not apply. It stops the session when the same call
repeats with nothing changed in between, asks the user after a streak of
failed calls, and ends the turn once spend read from the transcript passes
a dollar cap. It reads only new bytes (about 50 ms a call), fails open on
its own errors, never blocks if its folder goes missing, and installs and
uninstalls byte for byte.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Quote the skill path in sandbox-check and tool-design-checker commands

Skill folders can sit under paths with spaces, so every command that starts
from <skill-dir> quotes the script path.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Add tool-design-checker skill: will a model use your MCP tools correctly?

Grades MCP tool definitions the way a model meets them (clear purpose,
described parameters, safe annotations, size) against the smell categories
from arXiv:2602.14878 and Anthropic's tool-writing guidance. Authors point
it at a server or a tool list; users get every MCP server configured
across Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, and OpenCode, their token
load per harness, and tools that collide across servers. Starting servers
is opt-in; secrets from configs and the environment are masked in every
output, with a final redaction pass over the whole report.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Add rules-to-guards skill: enforce the AGENTS.md rules your agent breaks

Finds the checkable rules in AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, and GEMINI.md, counts
how often recent sessions broke each one, and turns the broken ones into a
tested hook for Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, or Cursor. The test step
replays the real violations (must block) and recent other commands (must
allow) before anything is installed, and installs merge with existing hooks.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Add session-waste-report skill: where your agent burns tokens and time

Reads Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, and OpenCode session logs and reports
the habits that waste spend (cache rebuilds after pauses, oversized tool
results, re-reads of unchanged files, polling loops) with dollar figures
that add up, plus a failure taxonomy (tool errors, denials, interrupts,
corrections, loops), each mapped to one fix. Leaves totals to ccusage.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Shared session parser: time windows, safe report text, cloud model prices

- unique_events(sessions, since=cutoff(days)) drops records older than the
  window: recently modified session files held months-old calls.
- safe_text() makes commands, paths, and transcript text one inert line
  for reports, so repository text cannot inject instructions or break tables.
- Claude Code's Monitor tool counts as a shell call.
- Bedrock and Vertex AI model ids get the model's list price, so a spend
  cap never counts them as $0.
- Project paths that are not UTF-8 no longer crash the Gemini CLI lookup.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Add sandbox-check skill: what your agent can really reach

Runs one probe through the agent's own shell and reports, headline first,
which secret files it can open, which files other programs later trust and
run (git hooks, shell startup files, harness settings), Docker, the SSH
agent, and sudo, then compares that with what the sandbox settings claim.
Reads no secret and edits no existing file; network checks only on request.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Add skill eval tooling and a shared session-log parser

skills/evals/tools/ vendors the lint, security scanner, trigger-routing,
and registry checks from Shubham Saboo's agent_skills collection
(awesome-llm-apps, Apache-2.0), with paths pointed at skills/.

skills/evals/shared/ holds the code six skills copy into their scripts:
transcripts.py reads Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, and OpenCode session
logs into one event shape (deduped per API response, forked sessions
counted once, untrusted text made safe for reports), and pricing.py
prices usage per model. sync_shared.py copies both and fails CI if a copy
drifts. Checked on real logs: computed Claude Code cost came to 98.2% of
Claude Code's own recorded cost across 11 sessions.

Stop recommending archived repos; label them in the tables

Flowise and Roo Code are archived upstream but kept in the ranked tables via
KEEP_DESPITE_ARCHIVED. That allowlist also let them through every use-case
filter, so Flowise was a top pick for "low-code / visual workflows" in the
README, FAQ, llms.txt, harnesses.json, the site, and MCP pick_harness.

- is_recommendable(): use-case picks now skip anything in ARCHIVED
- README rows show "archived upstream <date>"; guide line explains it
- harnesses.json projects carry "archived" (date or null)
- MCP _ranked skips archived projects for free-text queries too
